info.desc: 1988 liner notes for first CD issue Perhaps the most notable difference between the ways musicians and "fans" listen to jazz lies in the attention musicians pay to interaction. Jazzmen hear not only a soloist but an entire group playing together: the subtle difference between lackluster and brilliant performances. This is why musicians go into raptures over, say, the playing of bassist Sam Jones or pianist Hugh Lawson–raptures fans reserve for recognized "stars." Indeed, one frequently-discussed weakness of the current jazz scene is its relative lack of stable personnel, for normally even the most talented musicians need months or years .
